slides.title: Qwen2.5 1.5B Instruct
slides.body: Sweet spot between speed and quality on a single consumer GPU. Noticeably better reasoning and coding than the 0.5B.

slides.title: When to pick it
slides.body: Same guidance as the model details drawer — pick it for the right job.

cards.label: Great for
cards.text: Good default for local assistants, light coding help, and notebook experiments where 0.5B feels too weak but 3B is more than you need.

cards.label: Think twice for
cards.text: Very large-context workloads or frontier-level reasoning expectations.

slides.title: What's special?
slides.body: Same Qwen2.5 recipe as the flagship: ~18T-token pretraining, improved structured-output (JSON) generation, and multilingual coverage of 29+ languages — packed into a 1.5B checkpoint that typically fits in ~3GB of VRAM. It is often the best 'daily driver' small model when you want quality without a 7B download.
bullets: Scaling laws still apply inside a family — 1.5B sits on a steep part of the curve
Structured output (JSON) was an explicit Qwen2.5 training focus
Multilingual coverage is a first-class goal, not an afterthought

slides.title: Inside the model
slides.body: Dense Qwen2 decoder-only transformer with GQA, SwiGLU, RoPE, and the Qwen2.5 tokenizer/chat template. Same family design as 0.5B/3B — only width and depth scale.

flow.caption: Attention gathers context; the feed-forward layers transform it; the cycle repeats one token at a time.
